sources.use: Confirms existing church building purchased in April 2006 and current address at 1850 Woodland Avenue near Salisbury and Lindberg; no measured geometry.

Confirms renovated entry-to-sanctuary glass doors, lobby coffee bar/lounge, theatrical scrims/textured stage backdrop and childcare check-in canopies; portfolio photos are not scaled or georeferenced.

The selected 2022 exterior image shows red-brown brick, two dark flat canopies, stone piers and window bands; selected interior images show lounge/cafe materials and the sanctuary's chairs, stained-glass wall and timber frame.

sources.provider: Church and States independent blog (photographer not identified)
sources.use: Historical visual reference for the tall triangular stained-glass feature and broad entrance canopy; no location, scale, bearing or height is inferred from the photograph.

coordinate_system.project_frame: X east, Y north, Z up; meters; local approximate conversion
coordinate_system.uncertainty: This compatibility transform is not a surveyed coordinate reference system.

footprint_comparison.method: Project both four-corner rings into the project-local approximation; compare polygon area, intersection-over-union and symmetric boundary distances. This is a mapped-outline comparison, not a structural-wall survey.
footprint_comparison.interpretation: The 2018 lidar footprint is near-coincident but slightly larger. The difference could reflect outer eaves/roof capture or mapping differences; neither dataset labels the line as a surveyed structural wall. The stable OSM outline remains the wall-base reference, and a 0.45 m roof overhang is modeled separately.

measurements.wall_base_status: Retained the exact four-corner OSM ring in world XY; fresh-open nearest vertex error is recorded in reopen_validation.json.

modeled_height_m.status: All heights are visual estimates from photographs; no measured elevations or plan heights found.

measurements.bearing_status: Estimated from non-georeferenced images and the mapped site context; precise entrance bearing is unverified.
measurements.height_status: Estimated; neither OSM nor the state footprint layer supplies height or levels.

geometry_edits: Preserved the stable asset ID, object, collection, scene, file path and original OSM wall-base coordinates.

Rebuilt the one-box 16 m massing into a low red-brown brick church with a shallow charcoal gable roof, darker fascia, wall bands, clerestory/lower windows, and a prominent stained-glass A-frame gable.
Added grouped full-glass front doors, broad front canopy, two side entry canopies, limestone-colored support piers, frames and entrance base details from exterior photographs.
Added a schematic sanctuary beneath the stained-glass gable with a low stage, lectern, timber A-frame members and seven rows of upholstered chairs, oriented toward the gable.
Added a schematic lobby/cafe with wood floor, carpet zones, coffee counter, tables, lounge seating and connecting circulation, based on KJG's 2022 portfolio text and photos.
Applied project-scaled CC0 Poly Haven red-brick maps at 1.4 m UV tiling and packed color, normal, roughness and height textures into the standalone library.

brick.tint_note: Representative warm red-brown masonry; not a physical sample from Riverside.

materials.other_surfaces: Procedural stone, dark metal, glazing, wood, carpet and upholstery; texture dependencies packed or procedural.

validation.method: Blender 5.2.3 LTS fresh-open validation script checks stable identity, one-object collection export, source-ring corner agreement, metric UV layer and packed image dependencies.
validation.status: Stable manifest-path library reopened in Blender 5.2.3 LTS; stable ID, single-object export, exact OSM wall-base corners, metric UVs and packed textures all pass.

uncertainties: The named OSM footprint is not survey-grade; the independent Indiana lidar footprint is near-coincident but differs by up to about 1.46 m at boundary vertices, and its SHAPE__Area attribute is inconsistent with its returned geometry.
Roof overhang versus wall footprint is not distinguished by either GIS source; the current 0.45 m overhang is an estimate.
Exterior material tint, roof shape, window spacing, entry bearing, canopy dimensions and all heights are inferred from unscaled images.
The interior is a plausible visual layout based on architect photos, not a verified whole-building floor plan or measured room arrangement.
